title: Multi-region signed-cookie TTL discrepancy causes org-scope authorization drift
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: A production escalation from a Dedicated customer (Acme Analytics) reported intermittent 403s and, more severely, incorrect org scoping where requests from a user in org A were sometimes authorized against org B. Impact spanned Hosted and Dedicated deployments in multi-region setups and also surfaced for a small number of Private deployments using signed cookies for edge session affinity.

Root cause hypothesis: A mismatch in signed-cookie TTL normalization between the region edge (CDN/edge proxy) and origin token refresh logic permitted a short window where an expired signed cookie was still accepted by an edge node that had not received the latest token rotation state. This combined with a previously unseen edge sticky-route failover pattern caused the upstream to route requests to nodes that still accepted the stale cookie. Additionally, a bug in the org-binding reconciliation logic allowed an older session claim (with stale org mapping) to be reapplied during token refresh, causing temporary misattribution of tenant scope.

Why this is different from prior apikey rotation bugs: Previous incidents were primarily due to apikey cache windows and refresh races in the control plane. This incident ties together three pieces: edge cookie TTL normalization, signed-cookie signature verification path that bypasses full control-plane validation on cache hit, and org-binding reconciliation on refresh that can overwrite a current binding when encountering an older claim with a higher sequential id due to clock skew on dedicated hardware.

Immediate impact: Customer-facing traffic saw 1.8% of requests return 403 instead of 200 for a 48-hour window; for ~0.03% of requests there was transient cross-org data access (read-only) for up to 12 minutes per affected session before automatic reconciliation. This triggered an escalation and legal review request from the customer.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-11 22:40 UTC: Acme reported intermittent auth failures after they rotated their service keys as part of onboarding.
- 2026-03-12 01:10 UTC: On-call confirmed increased 403s correlated with rotation events in region eu-west-1 and us-east-1.
- 2026-03-12 04:00 UTC: Reproduced stale org-binding during a controlled rotation on a dedicated pool (internal test cluster).
- 2026-03-12 to 2026-03-13: Emergency mitigations applied (edge TTL alignment and temporary extended validation at origin).
- 2026-03-14: Ongoing development of code fix, tests, and review.
steps_to_reproduce: Provision a dedicated pool with multi-region edge nodes using signed cookies for session affinity.
Simulate a key rotation event that updates org mappings in the control plane while intentionally introducing a small clock skew on one region's control-plane agent.
Configure the CDN to use a different TTL normalization (rounding behavior) than the origin for signed-cookie expiry.
Send concurrent traffic during rotation and observe that some edge nodes accept the expired cookie and route to origin nodes with stale org-binding cache.
Observe org mismatch by querying /v1/session/inspect and comparing org_id in origin vs control-plane authoritative mapping.
proposed_fix: 1) Normalize signed-cookie TTL computation across edge and origin: move to server-side canonicalization function and publish as shared library used by edge config generator. 2) Harden origin verification: always perform a lightweight control-plane check for signed-cookie that are within a configurable grace window before accepting a claim for authorization decisions. 3) Prevent org-binding regressions on refresh by making reconciliation canonical & idempotent: accept newer mapping only when sequence numbers strictly increase and add an explicit safety check for clock skew. 4) Add a rollout plan with canary ratio and extra logging for any token rotation operations.
deployment_plan: Patch runtime and edge config generator, roll out to canary region (us-east-1) with 5% traffic for 6 hours; monitor auth/403 rate and org-mismatch alerts. If stable, increase canary to 25% for 3 hours, then 100% for region. Repeat for eu-west-1 and Private deployment customers during maintenance windows. Communicate with impacted customers and provide opt-in early patch for Dedicated pools.
qa_plan: Unit tests for TTL canonicalization and sequence-number check added to runtime test suite.
Integration tests that simulate rotation with intentional clock skew and CDN TTL mismatch in CI harness.
Staging canary with synthetic replay of Acme's traffic patterns (rotation frequency + traffic burst).
Manual verification steps for security team to validate no regression in signed-cookie revocation semantics.
rollback_plan: If increased org-mismatch or 403 rate > baseline + 0.5%, revert edge config generator change and runtime patch in the region; fall back to temporary mitigation: extend origin verification window and disable grace acceptance at edge. For Dedicated/Private, revert deployment to previous runtime image and run control-plane sync job to reconcile any lingering mappings.
monitoring: dashboards/auth/org-mismatch-rate - new metric that samples and compares origin vs control-plane org binding
audit-log stream for signed-cookie verification decisions (sampled at 1%)
